requirements.requires: the engine declares one refusal for a runtime identity that no longer matches the task's pin
requirements.why: Without a named refusal the mismatch has to be reported as something else, and a reader cannot tell a task parked for this reason from a task parked for any other. It is also the reason the plan's acceptance criteria name, so a rename here silently unmeets them.

requirements.requires: one function decides whether a task may proceed on the identity it is pinned to
requirements.why: Three call sites deciding this separately would drift: the fix that lands at enroll and not at dispatch is exactly the gap a task slips through, and it would look correct at each site read alone.

requirements.requires: a pin that cannot be read is refused rather than repaired or dropped
requirements.why: Repairing an unreadable pin re-admits the task on whatever the registry now holds, which is the outcome the pin exists to prevent. Dropping it is the same thing said more quietly.

requirements.requires: the decision runs when a task is enrolled
requirements.why: Enrolling is where a pin is written or honoured. Without the check here a task can be admitted onto code it was never pinned to, and every later check compares against that wrong pin.

requirements.requires: the decision runs when a task is resumed
requirements.why: A parked task resumes on whatever the registry now holds. This is the moment a refused identity would otherwise be laundered by waiting.

requirements.requires: the decision runs when the flow moves between two steps, and not only at enroll and resume
requirements.why: A registry can be swapped mid-session by an extension reload. A check at the two entry points alone lets a task admitted on one distribution finish on another, one step at a time. Anchored to the call rather than to the comment beside it, because a comment survives the deletion of the code it describes.

requirements.requires: the distribution digest the task was admitted under is compared against the one the registry serves now
requirements.why: This is the half of the lock that covers the bytes an extension was loaded from. Dropping it leaves the shape check alone, which passes whenever two different distributions declare the same steps.

requirements.requires: the declared workflow shape is compared as well as the distribution
requirements.why: The distribution digest covers the bytes, not what those bytes declared to the registry. A workflow assembled at load time from data outside its distribution can change its steps while the distribution stays identical, and only this comparison notices.

requirements.requires: a pin carrying no shape where the registry has one is refused rather than treated as covered
requirements.why: A pin written before shapes were recorded says nothing about the shape. Reading its silence as agreement would admit exactly the task the comparison above exists to stop, and it would do so for every task that predates the field.

requirements.requires: the declared shape has a digest of its own
requirements.why: Criterion 2 of issue #10 asks the graph digest to cover what the workflow is. This function is what produces it; without it the lock has only the distribution digest and the plan's criterion has nothing to bind to.

requirements.requires: the shape digest is computed from the canonical serialization, not merely alongside a function that could produce one
requirements.why: A digest over an incidental writing parks a good runtime as incompatible the first time a declaration is reformatted. Anchoring this to the declaration was the defect: a patch can leave `canonicalWorkflowGraph` standing and stop calling it, and the digest becomes whatever the new body returns while the declaration goes on satisfying the requirement.

requirements.requires: a workflow definition can carry the digest of the graph document it was built from
requirements.why: The declared shape covers steps and hook names and can cover nothing else: a transition, a guard, a cap and a resume target have no place in a declaration. Without this field the four components criterion 2 names are unreachable from the identity a task is pinned to, however faithfully the document declares them.

requirements.requires: the canonical shape serialises that digest, and serialises its absence too
requirements.why: Carrying the field without serialising it would leave the four components as far outside the identity as before. Writing a marker for absence is what makes adding the field to a workflow that had no document a change of shape rather than a silent no-op.

requirements.requires: the admission record takes the document digest off the definition instead of recomputing it
requirements.why: Recomputing would make two answers possible where the definition has one, and the shape digest already covers the same bytes. Both digests are written at one site because a second write site is how two projections of one definition drift apart.

requirements.requires: the admission's document digest is handed to the pin that gets written
requirements.why: Supply and persistence can both hold while the bridge between them is cut: an admission carrying the document and a writer able to persist it still produce pins without one if the call site drops the argument. This is the line where that would happen silently.
requirements.added_line: admitted: makePin(workflowName, current.distribution.digest, current.graph, helper, current.document),

requirements.requires: writing a pin persists the document digest when the pin carries one
requirements.why: Without the write the field never reaches disk, so every read finds it absent and the separate addressability is decoration. This is the more load-bearing half of the pair: the read below would still be present and the lock would pass while no pin ever carried a document.

requirements.requires: assigning the document into a pin survives at both sites that build one
requirements.why: The first anchor for this guarded the destructuring of the stored record, which a review showed leaves the whole lock green when the assignment into the result is deleted — the field would be read out of the record and thrown away. The assignment is the line that matters, and it exists twice: in the reader and in the pin builder. Both are pinned by one count, so losing either fails it.

requirements.requires: a document digest that is not a lowercase sha256 makes the pin malformed rather than tolerated
requirements.why: A pin is not defensively tolerated: a hand-forged or corrupt identity is the difference between running the code a task was enrolled on and running something else. A tolerated bad document would name a pair that never existed.
requirements.added_line: return { state: "malformed", reason: "runtime identity pin document is not a lowercase sha256" };

requirements.requires: every re-admit branch that builds a pin passes the document, not only the last one
requirements.why: A review found the document threaded through one of four pin-building call sites: first enroll and both re-admit branches wrote pins without it, so the field existed and the paths that create pins lost it. Three of the four share one line; this count is what notices one of them being dropped again.
requirements.added_line: admitted: makePin(workflowName, current.distribution.digest, current.graph, helper, current.document),

requirements.requires: applying a migration writes the target document into the pin it moves
requirements.why: A pin whose shape advanced while its document stayed behind names a pair that never existed. Without this line the receipt records a target document that no task was ever moved onto.

requirements.requires: the migration read-back compares the document as well as the shape
requirements.why: A read-back that checks only what the move wrote is a restatement of the move, not a verification of it. The shape and the digest were already compared; the document is the third component and its absence from the comparison would let a half-moved pin seal a receipt.

requirements.requires: reopening a migration whose plan matches but whose documents differ is refused
requirements.why: The documents are recorded and not identifying, so a second call with the same plan and different documents lands on the same receipt id. Returning it unchecked answers a request about one pair with a receipt describing another, and the apply that follows moves tasks onto the recorded document while the caller believes it asked for the other. Presence against absence is refused too: a receipt opened before the field existed cannot be retrofitted.
requirements.added_line: `migration ${id} was opened with ${name} ${was ?? "absent"} and is now asked for ${now ?? "absent"}`,

requirements.requires: the claimed source document is compared with the task's own before the move
requirements.why: The distribution digest cannot see it: a document can change inside one distribution, so a task whose document moved after the plan was opened passes that check while the receipt's claim about its origin is already false. After the move the true source is unrecoverable — read-back compares only the target — so this is the last point at which the claim can be tested.

requirements.requires: the canonical serialization sorts the steps
requirements.why: Step order carries no meaning to the engine, and `Object.entries` would not report the author's order for integer-like names in any case. Without the sort the digest would promise an order it cannot keep, holding for `intake`/`review` and quietly failing for `1`/`2`.

requirements.requires: applying a migration carries the store helper the task's pin already records into the pin it writes
requirements.why: The helper digests the binary that writes trusted state, not the extension, so a migration does not change it and the receipt cannot name one for it. Without the carry the apply writes a pin that every resume refuses as extension_version_mismatch for a missing store helper — a sealed migration whose tasks can never run. The read-back compares what the move carried, so deleting the line fails the apply instead of slipping a helper-less pin through.

requirement_growth.growth_rationale: The migration moved two of the pin's three identity components and dropped the third; the defect already shipped once, so the line that carries the store helper is anchored the way the document move already is.
